title: Bures-Isotropy Alignment: Manifold Learning of Generalized Category Discovery
claim: Conventional training collapses feature dimensions and mixes classes; our geometric regularizer restores a full, isotropic representation that separates known and novel categories.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, collapsed vs. isotropic sphere with eye icons
description: Two horizontal panels are stacked, (a) Conventional GCD on top and (b) Bures-Isotropy Alignment below, with a divider line between them. Each row follows the same flow. Two photos, a bear with a red border and a horse with a green border, feed through an encoder trapezoid labeled f. The encoder outputs a column of colored squares in a dashed box. In (a), only a few squares are colored (informative) and the rest are gray (collapsed). A double arrow links this column to a sphere where red, green and gray points are clumped together in the center, labeled 'with Dimensional Collapse'. Two eye icons with colored view cones point to a question mark. In (b), the colored fan-shaped beams from f show the token columns split into unknown and known groups. The sphere shows red and green points spread out and separated, labeled 'without Dimensional Collapse'. The eyes point to a red checkmark. The eye goes first to the photos on the left, then to the contrast between the clumped and spread spheres.
caption: (a) GCD is constrained by dimensional collapse due to strong clustering, leading to mixed class features and limited representational capacity. (b) BIA enhances the token geometry capacity, improving representational completeness and unlocking the model’s potential in the open world.
abstract: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) seeks to discover categories by clustering unlabeled samples that mix known and novel classes. While the prevailing recipe enforces compact clustering, this pursuit is largely blind to representation geometry: it over-compresses token manifolds, distorts eigen-structure, and yields brittle feature distributions that undermine discovery. We argue that GCD requires not more compression, but geometric restoration of an over-flattened feature space. Drawing inspiration from quantum information science, which similarly pursues representational completeness, we introduce Bures-Isotropy Alignment (BIA), which optimizes the mini-batch class-token Gram toward an isotropic prior by minimizing the Bures distance. Under a mild trace constraint, BIA admits a practical surrogate equivalent to maximizing the nuclear norm of stacked class tokens, thereby promoting isotropic, non-collapsed subspaces without altering architectures. The induced isotropy homogenizes the eigen-spectrum and raises the von Neumann entropy, improving both cluster separability and class-number estimation. BIA is plug-and-play, implemented in a few lines on unlabeled batches, and generally boosts strong GCD baselines on coarse- and fine-grained benchmarks, improving overall accuracy and reducing errors in the estimation of class-number. By restoring the geometry of token manifolds rather than compressing them blindly, BIA supplies compactness for known classes and cohesive emergence for novel ones, advancing robust open-world discovery. Code is available at github.com/lytang63/BIA.
